record.original_question: Is there an algorithm that computes a (1+epsilon)-approximation for job-shop makespan minimization J||C_max in time f(m, epsilon) * poly(n), depending on the number of machines m and approximation parameter epsilon but only polynomially on the input size?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13. Is there an algorithm that yields a (1 + ε)-approximation for J||Cmax in f(m, ε) · poly(n) time?
Job shop scheduling, denoted by “J” in the α-field: the operations of each job are totally ordered, yet each job may have a distinct total order on its operations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the job-shop scheduling problem with makespan objective, denoted J||C_max, defined as follows. We are given m machines M_1,...,M_m and n jobs J_1,...,J_n. Each job J_j consists of an ordered sequence of operations O_{j,1}, O_{j,2}, ..., O_{j,n_j}; each operation O_{j,k} must be processed non-preemptively on a prescribed machine μ(j,k) ∈ {M_1,...,M_m} for a prescribed integer time p_{j,k} > 0. A feasible schedule assigns to each operation O_{j,k} a starting time s_{j,k} ≥ 0 such that (i) for every job J_j and every k, s_{j,k+1} ≥ s_{j,k} + p_{j,k} (operations of a job are processed in the given order, without overlap), and (ii) for every machine M_i, the time intervals [s_{j,k}, s_{j,k}+p_{j,k}) over all operations with μ(j,k) = M_i are pairwise disjoint. The makespan is C_max = max_{j,k}(s_{j,k} + p_{j,k}), and the goal is to minimize C_max.

Let n denote the input size of an instance. Determine whether there exists an algorithm that, given any instance of J||C_max and any ε > 0, outputs a feasible schedule of makespan at most (1+ε)·OPT, where OPT is the optimum makespan, and runs in time f(m, ε) · poly(n) for some computable function f depending only on m and ε (i.e., a fixed-parameter tractable approximation scheme parameterized by the number of machines m, with only polynomial dependence on the rest of the input size).
artifact.status_search_result: The question asks whether J||C_max admits an FPT-approximation scheme parameterized by the number of machines m. Existing PTASs for job shop (Jansen–Solis-Oba–Sviridenko, and Feige–Scheideler's linear-time variant) require both the number of machines and the number of operations per job to be constant; no algorithm with running time f(m,ε)·poly(n) depending only on m and ε is known. Surveys on parameterized complexity of scheduling list this as an open problem, and no resolution was found in the literature search.

status_evidence.title: A Linear Time Approximation Scheme for the Job Shop Scheduling Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Linear time approximation schemes for both preemptive and non-preemptive job shop scheduling when the number of machines and the number of operations per job are fixed.
status_evidence.claim: Known PTAS results require both m and the maximum number of operations per job to be constant, not just m.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on parameterized/FPT-approximation for scheduling problems.
status_evidence.claim: FPT-approximation status for J||C_max parameterized by m is listed among open scheduling problems.

status_evidence.title: Hardness of Approximating Flow and Job Shop Scheduling Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Hardness results for flow and job shop scheduling.
status_evidence.claim: Hardness results indicate barriers to general approximation, motivating the parameterized question.
